evidence.quote: The spacecraft is intended to image and send data to ground stations for collation and analysis.
governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.reasoning: Covers primary mission (coral reef/ocean monitoring via fluid lensing), rationale (bleaching, GBR), single-spacecraft justification, and users (CSIRO/BOM, government/university). References [1]-[4] support claims. Detailed and persuasive, though some referencing is weak.

evidence.quote: an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924° for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous.
The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport.
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved

criteria.reasoning: Addresses launch, orbit, ground station, duration and EOL with STK screenshots and an inclination plot. But launch vehicle is unflown, Kourou-to-SSO dogleg ignored, access table has duplicate/inconsistent rows, no link budget, no software files, and Wikipedia used for launch data. Errors and missing detail place it at Adequate.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.

criteria.reasoning: Reaches specific conclusions on launch, orbit and ground station, but omits mission duration and EOL outcomes, and is somewhat generic. Adequate but not detailed.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

criteria.reasoning: Clear structure with headings and readable prose, but grammar errors ('a Earth', 'complied', 'purposed'), figures lack numbers, tables unlabelled, bibliography is bare URLs, and Wikipedia is cited. Presentation is adequate but not professional.

technical_issues.issue: Vega E is not yet operational (first launch 2024) and may not be available for 2025; launch from Kourou (5.05°N) to a 97.79° retrograde SSO requires a significant dogleg/plane change not discussed. Claim of 'two launch windows per day' is questionable.

RAAN 27.33° is said to indicate launch facility location; RAAN is not directly set by site latitude/longitude but by launch azimuth and time. No orbit maintenance (drag, J2) or station-keeping discussed.
STK access table contains a duplicate row 15 and row 6 has a 24-hour span but 365 s duration, indicating data inconsistency. No link budget or data-rate analysis.
Drag sail is proposed but not sized, and no demonstration of compliance with 25-year deorbit rule or deployment mechanism.
References are bare URLs without author/title/date; Wikipedia is used as a source [6], violating the no-Wikipedia requirement.
Figures have captions but no figure numbers; tables (launch, orbital elements, access) are unlabelled with table numbers/titles.

overall: A competent but flawed report. It covers all major mission elements with STK evidence and a coherent design, but technical gaps (launch dogleg, unflown vehicle, table errors, no link budget) and weak referencing/presentation reduce the mark. Weighted average approximately 6/10.
